methodology: The BareBoard Top 100 ranks devices by real-world use in 2026: active installed base and devices still in use today first, lifetime units sold second, from published figures only (company disclosures, official console sales, analyst reporting). Fact-checked 2026-10-15. Where no model-level figure is published, placement rests on category scale, distribution channel, production model, and longevity, and the entry's usage_evidence field says so — no figure is invented. The previous Hot 150 (v2.0) ranked by editorial hacker relevance; its bottom 50 under this usage ranking were removed on 2026-10-15 and preserved in Dropbox (/BareBoard-Site-Archive/hot-150-removed-bottom-50.json), with the full v2.0 file kept as hot150-original-v2.json.
ranking_basis: Real-world use in 2026 (installed base / units in use), from published figures. Higher rank = more devices in use today.

evidence_labels.confirmed: Multiple corroborating sources, including a published teardown.
evidence_labels.likely: At least one solid verifiable source (reference article or official product page).
evidence_labels.unconfirmed: Limited sourcing; official page unverified or thin corroboration.

selection_criteria: Device must have genuine hardware-hacker relevance (teardown interest, chip curiosity, repairability, or modding scene).
Device must have at least one verifiable public source URL.
No invented specifications, sales figures, or rankings.
Preference for devices with published teardowns or open hardware documentation.
Categories cover phones, SBCs, consoles, laptops, IoT, drones, VR, wearables, audio, tablets, networking, and hacker tools.

devices.usage_evidence: No figure published by Framework. The best-known repairable-laptop maker, selling globally since 2021 at a scale clearly above boutique Linux-laptop rivals — but orders of magnitude below MacBook/ThinkPad

devices.name: Framework Laptop 16
devices.why: 16-inch modular laptop with swappable GPU expansion bay.
devices.usage_evidence: No figure published. Newer (2024), larger and pricier than the 13 — the minority share of Framework's total. Close call — see flags

devices.name: Playdate
devices.why: Crank-controlled handheld; open SDK, beloved by indie devs.
devices.usage_evidence: Over 70,000 units sold (Panic; 53,142 by Apr 2023)

devices.name: Seeed XIAO ESP32S3
devices.why: A thumb-sized ESP32-S3 development board with an official manufacturer wiki covering pinout, power, and firmware, widely used as a teaching platform for embedded Wi-Fi and Bluetooth development.

sources.note: Official Seeed Studio getting-started wiki with hardware preparation and pinout documentation
Community getting-started guide with PlatformIO configuration and troubleshooting

devices.usage_evidence: No figure published. $5–8 board from Seeed's popular XIAO line, global distributor sales since 2023; cheap price drives volume, form factor limits it

devices.name: Arduino Nano ESP32
devices.why: The classic Nano form factor paired with an ESP32-S3 (u-blox NORA-W106), bridging the Arduino ecosystem with dual-core wireless silicon and serving as an accessible entry point to IoT hardware education.

sources.note: Technical report with full specifications of the NORA-W106 module, memory, and I/O
Pinout guide with tabulated specifications covering processor, memory, and power

devices.usage_evidence: No figure published. Arduino's official ESP32 board (2023), sold through Arduino's global education/retail channel — newer and pricier than clone ESP32 boards

devices.name: nRF52840 Dongle
devices.why: A low-cost Nordic USB reference design with castellated GPIOs that lets students inspect a real shipping BLE SoC implementation and program custom firmware onto it.

sources.note: PCA10059 specifications: SoC, protocols, GPIOs, antenna

devices.usage_evidence: No figure published. Nordic's low-cost official BLE dev dongle, a standard tool sold by all major electronics distributors since 2018

devices.name: Aqara Hub M3
devices.why: A multi-protocol Matter controller combining Zigbee, Thread border routing, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and an IR blaster, ideal for teaching how one gateway arbitrates several radio protocols.

sources.note: Official Aqara specs: Zigbee/Thread, PoE, IR blaster, Wi-Fi 802.11 a/b/g/n/ac
Official Aqara comparison of Zigbee 3.0, Thread and Matter protocol support

devices.usage_evidence: No model figure. Aqara is a mass-market smart-home brand (Xiaomi ecosystem, Apple/Amazon retail); M3 is its 2024 flagship hub — a hub is one-per-home, capping units. Close call — see flags
